purpose: Test whether broad cross-sectional participation contains incremental after-cost information about subsequent crypto-market direction that was absent from the rejected basis and realized-funding fingerprints.

source.data_family: completed timestamp-safe OHLC candles already available to research

immutable_feature.name: pit_cross_sectional_breadth_24h
immutable_feature.definition: 2 * (count of point-in-time eligible assets with strictly positive trailing 24h close-to-close return / count of point-in-time eligible assets with valid trailing 24h return) - 1
immutable_feature.point_in_time_eligibility: Use the repository canonical point-in-time universe at each forecast timestamp; never construct the cohort from present-day survival or future liquidity.

hypothesis.primary_question: Does pre-forecast 24h market breadth add stable incremental after-cost information for 24h or 7d crypto-market direction/return beyond a frozen training-only constant-direction baseline?
hypothesis.economic_mechanism: Broad participation may distinguish durable market-wide demand/supply from narrow moves driven by a few leaders; if real, that should improve subsequent market-direction expectancy rather than merely describe contemporaneous price strength.
hypothesis.direction_rule: Learn only the sign of the breadth/forward-return association from the chronological training segment and freeze it before OOS scoring; do not tune a breadth cutoff on validation or OOS.

evaluation_contract.target: equal-weight return of the same point-in-time eligible market cohort over the primary horizon, computed only as the future label

rejection_rules: reject if the canonical point-in-time universe cannot be reconstructed without future information
reject if fewer than 15 eligible assets are available at a scoring timestamp
reject if fewer than 8 independent OOS samples remain for either scored primary horizon
reject if canonical after-cost OOS expectancy is non-positive
reject if incremental OOS expectancy versus the frozen training-only constant-direction baseline is non-positive or unstable
reject if apparent edge disappears under fixed 2x/3x cost stress
reject if OOS halves, liquidity cohorts, or universe-size stability checks materially contradict the claimed edge
reject if breadth is redundant with already-tested momentum evidence and adds no incremental economic value
forbidden_actions: do not use a present-day fixed survivor list to manufacture historical breadth
do not retry unchanged Binance historical-OI route
do not retry unchanged Bybit historical-OI route
do not tune breadth thresholds or lookbacks from OOS outcomes
do not combine breadth with dispersion, residual momentum, regime filters, or other features inside this fingerprint
do not open untouched OOS from this candidate-selection step
do not create paper, broker, promotion, or live-trading authority

why_ranked_next.profitability_first: Uses existing zero-incremental-cost data to test a different economic mechanism that can potentially suppress narrow, fragile market-direction trades and improve dollars earned per unit risk.
why_ranked_next.information_value: A clean rejection is valuable because it determines whether simple broad participation deserves further investment before adding more complex cross-sectional interactions.

next_step: Implement the smallest bounded evaluator for this frozen fingerprint and falsify it chronologically before adding any breadth variants or interactions.
